lesson_title: The Worm That Becomes a Moth
hook_text: Mopane worms are not worms at all. Wait until you see what they turn into.
clip_script: Summer in Giyani. Fat, spotted mopane worms munch mopane leaves. Families collect them to cook. But leave a few! A full-grown worm crawls down, digs into the soil and becomes a pupa. Months later, after the rains, out climbs a huge emperor moth. It lays eggs on a mopane tree. The eggs hatch into tiny caterpillars. Egg, caterpillar, pupa, moth, and round again. That is a life cycle.
visual_style: Whiteboard circle of four pictures: eggs on a leaf, a caterpillar, a pupa in the soil and a moth, linked by arrows.
mood: Surprising and proud of local knowledge.
pacing: Start with the familiar worm, follow it underground, reveal the moth, close the circle.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the life cycle of an animal you know.
